Revels and Bruce were both members of the Republican Party.

The ruling, which could affect similar laws in other British Commonwealth countries, has spotlighted a legal system still intertwined with a former colonial power. The 19-year-old Bulgarian racing driver will join a TPC session in Hungary this week. A TPC programme allows F1 teams to run cars from previous seasons. It is usually held in private, giving current drivers, reserve drivers, and young prospects more experience behind the wheel. For reserve drivers, a TPC helps ensure that they are up to par with real F1 machinery, not just the simulators that they typically practice on. Then, for prospects like Tsolov, a session gives F1 engineers the opportunity to observe how young drivers adapt to F1 cars and communicate technical feedback. The TPC can help them understand tyre management, braking, steering inputs, and car behavior.

The American Cancer Society is recommending routine prostate cancer screening for more middle-aged men, in a major change to its guidelines. Middle-aged men should undergo regular screening for prostate cancer, the American Cancer Society said Thursday in a major change to its guidelines. The screening involves a simple blood test, and men at average risk of getting prostate cancer should receive the prostate-specific antigen, or PSA, test every two years between the ages of 50 and 69, the cancer society advised. Men at high risk, including Black men and men with a strong family history of prostate cancer, should get yearly PSA checks and start earlier, at age 45.

French heptathlete Auriana Lazraq-Khlass is suspended for 22 months for failing to comply with anti-doping rules. Major global companies including Bally's and Betano were swapped out, replaced by tech, tourism, and financial services firms. Others, including Stake, were moved to shirt sleeves. Heinz von Foerster thought population would grow exponentially and "squeeze" us all to death. It’s not a new fear. English economist Thomas Malthus —one of the early pioneers in modeling population dynamics—made a similar prediction in 1798, claiming that a rapidly growing population would eventually exhaust the available food supply, and humanity would starve to death. His model rested on the assumption of exponential growth, but the equation is only applicable under specific conditions, such as scientists growing bacteria in a lab in a perfectly controlled environment. Even then, while growth occurs exponentially for a time, it does not continue forever.

The Federal Reserve will vote on interest rates less frequently beginning next year as part of a plan by the central bank’s chairman, Kevin M. Warsh, to overhaul how it operates. SignDrop" exploit lets local users gain all-powerful System rights. On Tuesday, Nightmare Eclipse disclosed SignDrop, a vulnerability that gives local users full System rights on some versions of Windows. The vulnerability resides in the Common Log File System , which Microsoft describes as a “general-purpose logging service used by software clients running in user-mode or kernel-mode.” By forcing a privileged process such as Windows Defender to open a crafted CLFS container, an attacker with ordinary user rights can abuse the privileged file creation to elevate privileges to System.

No PGA Tour player is as tied professionally to Dan Hicks as is Tiger Woods. Hicks was on the call for many of Woods' victories, but none more memorable than the 2008 U.S. Open, when Woods made a birdie putt on the 72nd hole to force a Monday playoff with Rocco Mediate at Torrey Pines (which Woods won). "Expect anything different?" Hicks exclaimed after the putt circled in. Those three words are among the most famous in golf broadcast history. Hicks died Wednesday at age 64, with news of his passing reaching the public on Thursday. Woods expressed his sadness, admiration for Hicks and sympathy for Hicks' family, including wife Hannah Storm, in a social post Friday afternoon.

Cost and access barriers are pushing people to modified use and unapproved versions. In a study published this week , researchers at the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention broke down survey data of GLP-1 use collected between July and August of 2025. Based on responses from over 8,000 US adults, the researchers estimate that about one in 10 US adults (9.8 percent) used a glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist, aka GLP-1 medication, in 2025. That’s around 27 million adults. The study was published in the CDC’s Morbidity and Mortality Weekly Report.

To win a Senate seat in a highly polarized, deeply Republican state, Scott Colom needed a perfect storm. He got it. To pull off Mississippi’s first Democratic Senate victory in more than four decades — in a state Donald J. Trump won by nearly 23 percentage points just two years ago — Scott Colom couldn’t simply ride a shifting national mood over the finish line. A win would require high turnout among Black voters, who make up nearly 40 percent of the state’s population, and inroads with white voters. It also would not hurt if his opponent, Senator Cindy Hyde-Smith, did worse than other Republicans on the ballot, as she had in the past.
